study_identification_part.si4_title: Age-atypical brain functional networks in autism spectrum disorder: a normative modeling approach

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The study clearly states its aims: (1) define age-varying normative values of within- and between-network functional connectivity (FC) and mark extremes (>2 SD), (2) provide individual-level assessment relative to population norms across age, and (3) examine relationships between deviation scores (W-scores) and ASD symptoms. It also articulates the purpose of normative modeling to address heterogeneity and move beyond mean case-control differences.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: We aimed (1) to determine a predicted normative value of within- and between-network FC that changes with age... (2) to provide an individual-level assessment... (3) to elucidate the relationship between brain data and symptoms...

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: The reference cohort (TD) comes from ABIDE. The authors cite ABIDE as the data source and describe exclusion criteria (left-handed participants and poor scan quality). They report final sample size after exclusions (TD n=642). Image quality screening is mentioned via exclusion of poor scan quality.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: All the data analyzed in this study were sourced from the ABIDE dataset... we excluded left-handed participants and those with poor scan quality. After exclusion, the sample size was 642 for the TD group and 576 for the ASD group.

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: Age is explicitly modeled as the key covariate in the normative model. Multi-site effects are addressed via ComBat harmonization. However, sex is not modeled as a covariate in the normative fitting, so not all typical covariates are covered.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: This enables prediction of the FC value ... from the clinical covariates (age)... Multisite effect correction: Site effects ... were removed using the ComBat function...

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: The statistical approach is described: local polynomial regression (LOESS) with hyperparameter optimization (Brent's method via R stats::optim). Alternative model (Gaussian process regression) considered and rationale for choosing LOESS provided in supplement. Software/libraries (R) are referenced.
